items.title: 白背景の画像が重いとき、PNGのまま配る前に確認すること
items.summary: 白い背景の写真が重いとき、背景が単純だから小さくなるはずだと考えてしまう。しかしファイルサイズは、画像の内容、画素数、形式、圧縮設定によって変わる。見た目の白さと、配信するデータ量は分けて確認したい。 まず配信されている寸法を見る 表示幅が小さいカードに、数千ピクセルの原画像を送っていないかを調べる。ブラウザーの表示サイズだけではなく、ネットワーク上で取得した画像の寸法を確認する。CSSで縮めても、送られるファイルが自動的に小さくなるわけではない。 高密度ディスプレイへの対応も必要だが、すべての場所へ最大の画像を送る理由にはならない。必要なバリエーションを決め、実際のカード幅と画面密...
items.titleJa: 白背景の画像が重いとき、PNGのまま配る前に確認すること
items.summaryJa: 白背景の画像は見た目の白さだけでなく内容や解像度、圧縮設定などでファイル容量が決まるため、表示サイズだけでなく実際に取得した寸法や容量を確認する必要がある。配信用には元ファイルを保存して別に最適化版を作成し、背景処理と圧縮を分けて検討、透明度や質感の保持を考慮して候補形式を比較する。最終的には採用理由を記録し、素材ごとに比較条件を残して次回に活かせるようにする。

items.title: CSS Optimization: Is Using Declarations Just Once (UDJO) Still Effective Today?
items.summary: Is the technique inspired by the DRY principle by identifying and reducing (if not eliminating) CSS declaration repetition still a relevant optimization strategy? CSS Optimization: Is Using Declarations Just Once (UDJO) Still Effective Today? originally handwritten and published with love on CSS-Tricks . You should really get the newsletter as well.
items.titleJa: CSS Optimization: Is Using Declarations Just Once (UDJO) Still Effective Today?
items.summaryJa: UDJO（ declarations just once）は、古くからのDRY原則に基づくCSSの重複削減手法で、宣言の繰り返しをまとめてスタイルの保守性とファイルサイズの削減を目指す。著者は20サイト以上の検証を通じ、UDJOが必ずしもファイルサイズを削減するとは限らないケースがある一方で、適切なデータとツールを用いれば多くの場合でサイズ削減につながると結論づけている。つまり、UDJOは現代のCSS最適化において有効であり得る手法として、保守性とパフォーマンスの両方を念頭に導入すべきだと示唆している。

items.titleJa: 耳で聞く！Python で学ぶ マクロ経済学 入門 43
items.summaryJa:
本動画は、Qiita記事「大学の運営費削減と任期付きポジションが需要を冷やすメカニズム」を対話形式で深掘りしたもので、基盤費を削って競争的資金に依存させる政策が、長期的には研究力とマクロ経済需要を悪化させるという結論を数学的に示しています。マクロ経済的には、安定した雇用・研究環境を「エンジン」として整備することが不可欠だと主張し、教育・科学技術・人的資本の重要性を位置づけています。

items.title: Decision models take 26% of requests; Anthropic now wins new teams 2:1
items.summary: AI Gateway Production Index — November 2026 Every month, AI Gateway routes more than 100 trillion tokens between production applications and AI labs. That traffic gives us a view of what AI usage looks like in today’s enterprise and startup landscape across language, decision, voice, image, and video models. We publish it here monthly. See the Production Index reports from August , September , and October . November 2026 Summary In six weeks, decision models grew to one in four gateway requests, while accounting for half a cent of every dollar spent. Close to a third of all paid teams used one in October. Among teams processing over 10 billion tokens a month, seven in ten used a decision model. About 11% of paid teams used a voice model in October, up from 4% in July. OpenAI and Anthropic now reach about the same share of paid teams, and new teams in October picked Anthropic nearly two to one . OpenAI’s share of gateway spend, meanwhile, is up by two-thirds since December. More than half of language-model requests went to models less than two months old, up from less than three in ten. Within one month of a typical model’s peak usage, three in four of the teams using it have moved on. Decision models account for 26% of all requests Production AI is splitting into two jobs: generation and judgment. Until recently, when software needed to make a quick call, a team could use either a fixed rule that was cheap but rigid, or a language model that was smart but slow and expensive. Decision models are now a third option. They classify, score, or pick between choices instead of generating text, and cost about a seventieth as much per request as a language model. They arrived on AI Gateway in mid-September, and there are now 15 decision models available from eight different vendors. In October, nearly a third of paid teams on AI Gateway used a decision model. About 11% of paid teams used a decision model without sending a single request to a text-generating model. Decision models cost far less per token and give very short answers, so even though they received about one in four gateway requests in October, they accounted for just 0.53% of total spend. Almost all of that request volume went to Jev from TypeSafe AI, which alone received nearly four times Anthropic’s total requests. For every $1 teams spent on Jev, they spent $64 on Anthropic models. Decision models are most common among the teams that run the most AI. Just over one in five teams running fewer than 10 million tokens used a decision model in October. At 100 million to 1 billion tokens, nearly half used one. Above 10 billion, seven in ten did. This is partly because big teams use more of everything. The top 1% of teams by spend use a median of 29 different models, and the bottom tenth use only one. It’s also volume. The more requests a team sends, the more it has to gain from a model that makes simple decisions faster and far more cost-effectively. Voice adoption is up 2.6x since July About one in nine paid teams used a voice model in October, up from one in 24 in July, an increase of 161%. New teams are using voice, and existing teams are adding it. Among teams that paid in both July and October, the share using voice went from 5% to 14%. Teams that use voice are also using more of it. The share of teams sending at least 100 voice requests a month grew fivefold, and six in ten of September’s voice teams returned in October, up from fewer than half in July. A spoken conversation with an AI app takes three steps: A voice model turns the user’s speech into text A language model writes the reply Another voice model reads the reply back to the user Most voice teams use just one or two of these pieces. Use of speech-to-text models has nearly tripled since July, and text-to-speech has more than tripled. Some models do all three steps on their own. In July, about a quarter of voice teams used one of these all-in-one models, and one in six assembled the pieces themselves. By October, those numbers had swapped. For most teams, voice is a new way for users to talk to an app or agent they already have. Teams’ preferred language models stay in the middle, and they can add voice at one end or both. Anthropic wins new teams two to one, and OpenAI’s share of spend is up two-thirds Last December, 70 of every 100 paid teams on AI Gateway used an OpenAI model and 48 used an Anthropic model. By October, the two labs were nearly level, with OpenAI at 55 and Anthropic at 54. Both labs now reach more of the teams that have been on the gateway since December, but Anthropic’s reach grew more. The share of these teams using Anthropic rose from about half to two-thirds, while OpenAI’s rose from about three in four to four in five. Most of Anthropic’s gain came from new teams. In October, it was the first-choice lab for nearly twice as many of them as OpenAI. But among the biggest teams, both labs already have nearly everyone. More than nine in ten of the top 1% by spend use both Anthropic and OpenAI. With these teams, the labs now compete for how much of the work each one gets. On that measure, Anthropic still leads, but OpenAI has gained ground. OpenAI now takes nearly 15 cents of every dollar spent on the gateway, up from about 9 in December, while Anthropic’s halved to about 32 cents over the same period. Most AI traffic now runs on models less than two months old Teams are moving to new models almost as fast as labs release them. More than half of October’s language-model requests went to models less than 60 days old. Before September, that share had never passed three in ten. Within each model family, a new version arrives every 61 days at the median, and a typical model peaks within a month of launch. Four weeks later, three in four of the teams using it at its peak aren’t using it anymore, whether or not a successor has shipped in the family. Most of those teams are still on AI Gateway, using other models. Teams switch models frequently, usually to something newer, and often to another lab. In October, about half of teams running at least 10 million tokens a month changed their most-used model. Four in five of those moved to a more recent release, and six in ten moved to a different lab. Older models stay in use, often alongside a newer primary model. Seven in ten teams running at least 10 million tokens a month still used a model at least ten months old in October, but for the typical team it ran less than 3% of its tokens. AI models now have a half-life of about six weeks. That means that, to the teams using them, labs are only as good as their latest model and have to re-earn their business with every new one. Also in October’s data Opus 5.5 was the top model by spend in its first full month. It took about one in seven dollars across all teams. Four of the six most widely used models on AI Gateway are Anthropic’s: Sonnet 5.5 (reaching 26% of paid teams), Haiku 5.5 (22%), Haiku 4.5 (20%), and Opus 5.5 (18%). Jev (28%) and GPT-6 Luna (19%) are the other two. Image and video both had their biggest month yet on AI Gateway. More teams than ever are putting spend on them, and the largest teams are adopting them the fastest. About a third of the top 1% of teams by spend now use an image model, up from a quarter in July. One in six use a video model, up from one in ten. OpenAI’s newest image model, GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst, took the lead in image spend in its first full month, followed by its Flare and GPT-Image-2 models. ByteDance’s Seedance 2.5 led video spend for a third month running, ahead of Google’s Veo 3.1 and Kuaishou’s Kling 3.0. About this data This report uses anonymized, aggregate traffic routed through Vercel AI Gateway through October 2026. A few notes on measurement: Spend is estimated at published list prices; actual bills may differ. Paid teams are teams with at least one paid request in the month. Team size is measured by a team’s total tokens that month. Decision models are the models classified as decision models in the AI Gateway model list. Each model version is counted separately. A model’s age is measured from that version’s first day on AI Gateway, and gateway history begins October 20, 2025. Switching rates compare paid teams with at least 10 million tokens in both September and October. A team’s most-used model is measured by tokens. Voice figures begin June 22, 2026. Teams that “assembled the pieces” used speech-to-text, a language model, and text-to-speech on the same day. A new team’s first-choice lab is the lab it sent the most language-model requests to in its first month. All figures use the most recent data and protocol available; prior months may be revised as methodology is updated. Read more about our methodology , and explore or download the public data . items.summaryJa: Chrome 157でHTML-in-Canvasが正式実装され、2D/WebGL/WebGPUでDOM要素を描画する際もテキスト選択やページ内検索、翻訳などが機能することを検証した。日本語縦書きテキストを題材に、歪んだテクスチャ上での選択・コピー、翻訳、Ctrl/Cmd+Fのハイライト、CSS変更の即時反映、描画コスト、縦書き・禁則・ルビの表示、動画出力、同一オリジン/別オリジンの画像の挙動を検証した。結論として、1〜7は動作を確認でき、8は別オリジンでCORSなしの場合は描画されず無言になる制約である。実装はWebGL2で行い、デモは antymark.com/demo/html-in-canvas/ で公開されている。

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 from Anthropic is now available on AI Gateway . Fable 5.2 is built for open-ended technical work and improves on earlier Fable models in coding, reasoning, and vision. It can run long, ambiguous tasks unattended, and works as an orchestrator that hands simpler tasks to smaller models, or as an advisor that other Claude models consult on harder problems. It also communicates more clearly and generates output faster than earlier Fable models. Effort runs from low to max , with high as the API default. Fable 5.2 has cybersecurity and biology safety classifiers enabled. Access to Claude Fable 5.2 requires data retention. Anthropic does not support Zero Data Retention for the model. Prompts and completions are retained for 30 days and are not used to train Claude. If your team has ZDR turned on, AI Gateway returns an error instead of sending the request to Fable 5.2. To keep requests served when a classifier is triggered, use model fallbacks . Add a models array to providerOptions.gateway , and AI Gateway tries each model in order when the cybersecurity classifier declines a request. Call it through the AI SDK , the Chat Completions , Responses , and Anthropic Messages APIs, or a coding agent connected to AI Gateway. Use anthropic/claude-fable-5.2 as the model name: This request falls back to Opus 5.5, then Sonnet 5.5, if the cybersecurity classifier declines it. The models option works the same way on every AI Gateway API format. To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Try Claude Fable 5.2 in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. items.summary: Muse Ember from Meta is now available on AI Gateway . Muse Ember handles the bounded tasks agents repeat many times in a single run, like implementing a helper function, calling a tool, or summarizing a document. The model accepts text, image, and video input with a 1M-token context window, so an agent can pass it code, screenshots, documents, and clips in the same run. Tool calling lets your application feed each result into the next step. Reasoning effort is adjustable from minimal to max .
